story.approach:
My approach at Chef Ima was focused on making marketing more commercially effective.

Rather than treating marketing as an isolated promotional function, I worked on improving the relationship between customer acquisition, sales activities and repeat business.

I restructured aspects of the sales and marketing operations, developed customer offers and retention packages, and implemented acquisition campaigns designed to attract new customers while encouraging existing customers to return.

I also focused on making the business's marketing activities more intentional, ensuring that promotional efforts were connected to revenue generation and business performance.

This experience helped me develop a stronger understanding of marketing as a commercial function, rather than simply a communications or visibility tool.
story.overview: Led and restructured marketing and customer acquisition activities for a growing food business, with a focus on improving sales performance, customer retention and profitability.
story.challenge:
Chef Ima was one of the engagements where I developed a stronger foundation in marketing as a professional discipline.

My work went beyond running campaigns. I examined the business's existing sales and marketing processes, identified weaknesses and helped restructure its commercial approach.

This included developing new customer offers, acquisition campaigns, messaging and retention initiatives.
story.contribution:
As Marketing Lead, I led:
- Marketing strategy and brand positioning.
- Customer acquisition campaigns.
- Offer development.
- Sales and marketing process improvements.
- Customer retention and repeat-purchase initiatives.
- Marketing execution and performance improvement.
story.results: The revised commercial structure contributed to approximately 40% profit growth within six months, according to the business records referenced in your CV.
story.lessons:
Working at Chef Ima taught me that marketing is only one part of business growth.

A company can attract attention and generate interest, but without a functioning sales process, a clear commercial model and the ability to convert opportunities into revenue, growth becomes difficult to sustain.

I began to understand that scaling a business requires the different parts of its commercial operation to work together.

That lesson has remained central to how I think about business development and go-to-market execution today.
